issues.corrective_action: Search integer nurse splits systematically, ordered by L3, then L2-3, then total covered need, before submitting.
issues.impact: About 0.15 nurse-units of L2 need left uncovered (orthopedics L2 short 0.65 versus cardiology L2 short 0.5 under the alternative).
issues.principle: Nurses cover higher levels first; efficiency requires the best covered need within the pool.
issues.what_happened: Nurses were split CA13/IM10/NE8/OR6. This covers L2-3 need of 12.5+9.8+8.0+6.0 = 36.3 nurse-units. L3 need (23.4) is fully covered.
issues.what_should_have_happened: A split of CA12/IM10/NE8/OR7 also covers all L3 need and covers 12.0+9.8+8.0+6.65 = 36.45 at levels 2-3, which is higher. The chosen split should have moved one nurse from cardiology to orthopedics.
issues.why_incorrect: With equal L3 coverage, another whole-number split of the same 37 nurses covers more L2-3 need, so the split was not the best. The explanation compared only the 12/10/9/6 alternative and never tested 12/10/8/7.

report.summary: All five allocations were valid, with no rejected submissions or failure days. Clinical priority was respected: only L1 patients waited, no L2 or L3 patient was left without a bed, and L3 nursing was fully covered every day. I found no bed displacement or fairness inversion. One nurse gap (day 30, Moderate) and one explanation misstatement (day 27, Moderate) were found. Frequent bed and nurse moves between departments were reversed within 3 days (Minor); I counted them with oldest-first matching, and the matching of individual units is ambiguous in a few cases. Explanations were otherwise accurate against the records. Some tool-computed alternatives were incomplete.
